The abstract states that determination of prospective teachers' metaphoric perceptions of science education will contribute to the more effective and efficient organization of science education and the organization and structure of its teaching.
The research aimed at determining prospective teachers' metaphoric perceptions toward science education in terms of various variables.
The research was conducted on 301 prospective teachers.
The research adopted a phenomenological study, which is one of the qualitative research designs.
A creative comparison form was used as a data collection tool.
The content analysis method, which is one of the qualitative data analysis methods, was used to analyze the collected data.

As a result of the study, the creative comparisons of prospective teachers for science education were gathered under 5 categories: emotion, color, game, transportation vehicle, and technological tool.
Prospective teachers produced several metaphors according to these categories.
Some suggestions were made based on the results.
The keywords are Creative comparisons, phenomenology, prospective teachers, science education.
The document states that in the Turkish education system, science lessons have been more difficult for students to understand than other lessons every semester (Yılmaz & Batdı, 2016).

The document states that for this reason, in science education, it is important to increasingly concretize the abstract expressions, which are difficult to understand, with different methods and techniques, and to make them easier to understand (Arslan & Bayrakçı 2006; Hançer et al., 2007).

The document states that to overcome these difficulties, researchers have made use of simulation, analogy, animation and simulations, and various methods and techniques such as concept maps, conceptual change texts, the six thinking hats technique, station project-based, cooperative learning, and 5E teaching model.
The document states that the main objective is to raise science-literate individuals within the science education program of the students (MNE, 2018).
The document states that science literacy requires individuals to understand and use the scientific concepts in the social, cultural, economic and decision-making process.
The document states that one of the important dimensions of science literacy is to learn the scientific concepts.

The document states that concept learning is important in creating scientific principles by classifying the structures with similar characteristics and associating them with other concepts (Çepni et al., 1997).

The document states that in today's understanding, teaching of the Science course is based on making the information meaningful and experiential for the students rather than the evaluation of the student's level of knowledge (MNE, 2018).
The document states that the most important aim of the Science course is to train students to be science-literate.
